_: GENERATED by scripts/build-tokens.mjs. Do not hand-edit.
Layer 1 of the design system: everything that is NOT a colour.
Hand-edit this file. Everything downstream — core.css, each set's
tailwind.config.js, each app's global.css, each app's theme/tokens.ts — is
emitted from it by scripts/build-tokens.mjs and must never be edited
directly. Lint check 11 regenerates and diffs, so a hand edit is caught.
TWO SURFACES, ONE SYSTEM.
A 390px phone frame and a 1120px web page do not want the same type scale:
the phone wants fixed px steps, the page wants fluid rem clamps. Forcing
one on the other would be a worse system, not a more unified one. So the
metric scales are per surface and everything that actually causes drift is
shared — the naming rule, the colour key set, the role semantics, the
reserved-block discipline, and the lint that checks all of it.
Provenance is recorded per block. Where sets disagreed, the note says who
won and why, so the next person does not re-litigate it from scratch.

font._: All six token-driven mobile sets declared this identical pair. No mobile app loads a webfont; three declare expo-font and never import it. The web surface adds display/sans/mono via next/font on top of these fallbacks.

_: Geometry is shared across surfaces; tint and strength are per product.
Two geometry families existed on mobile — 14px/34px -10px (aakalan,
askcal, imposter) and 12px/30px -8px (charades, plan-kid) — with
tic-tac-toe on a third. The first wins on count.
A product supplies --shadow-tint as an `r g b` triple and may override
--shadow-a1/a2/a3. A dark product needs a far heavier alpha to read at
all, which is why strength is a variable rather than baked in.
Pinned. Every one of the 572 Tailwind loads and 159 lucide loads in
the tree was unpinned — bare cdn.tailwindcss.com and lucide@latest — so
no design set rendered reproducibly and a CDN release could silently
restyle 452 screens. Lint check 9 enforces these exact URLs.
The canonical colour key set. A palette declaring a key outside this
list, or a ramp stop outside `rampStops`, fails lint check 3.
Only brand-500 is required. Seven-stop ramps are the norm and the
drift page reports completeness, but forcing ten stops would mean
inventing hexes nobody designed — tic-tac-toe genuinely has one.

renamed._: Old name -> canonical name. The lint reports any survivor so a missed rename is visible rather than silently painting nothing.

mobile._: The 390x844 phone frame the wireframes are drawn in, and the Expo apps behind them.

_: The four wireframe steps were byte-identical in all six token-driven
sets — the strongest shared convention in the tree. The product scale
is imposter's, the only app that had one.
Emitting this into every runtime global.css is what makes `text-2xs`
live: it is used 186 times across aakalan, askcal and charades and was
declared in none of them.
tic-tac-toe's h1 was 34px and moves to 36px — two apps had a product
scale and they disagreed on exactly one step.

tracking._: 0.18em, from aakalan / askcal / imposter / tic-tac-toe. charades and plan-kid declared 0.15em in config while hard-coding 0.18em in their own .section-label, so they already contradicted themselves and lose nothing. `role` is imposter's and stays reserved to it.
tracking.label: 0.18em

_: Unanimous except tic-tac-toe's 2xl, which was 28px where every sibling
had 24px — so `rounded-2xl` rendered differently in exactly one app.
`phone` was a token in askcal / charades / plan-kid and a hard-coded
40px inside a media query in aakalan / imposter. Now a token
everywhere. chitragupt and property-app used 32px and move to 40px.

shadow._: Inherits shared.shadowGeometry and adds the desktop frame, which only exists on a wireframe page.

frame._: 390x844 is already the house rule in apps/CLAUDE.md. The desktop breakpoint is where the frame gains its rounded body and drop shadow.

_: ritesh-firodiya.github.io and the other web surfaces. Fluid rem clamps,
not the phone's fixed px — a heading that is 36px on a 390px frame and
36px on a 1440px page is wrong on one of them.
These are the live values already shipping in src/app/globals.css. They
are lifted here unchanged so the site stops being a twelfth system and
becomes the one the others are measured against.

tracking._: 0.14em, not the phone's 0.18em. A label set in a 70rem column needs less air than the same label in a 390px frame.
tracking.label: 0.14em

spacing._: Only ever used as padding. Halved in Sep 2026; the utilities .px-gutter / .py-section wrap them.

palettes.name: aakalan
_: Reference implementation of the two-theme rule. aakalan was the only set
in the tree with a complete dark palette — every token has a dark value,
including all seven category pairs and all four status trios.
Renames applied: indigo-* -> brand-*, saffron-* -> accent-*,
--text-primary -> --ink, --border -> --line, --page-bg -> --page.
Values are unchanged; a retoken here must be invisible on screen.
Money direction is a different axis from success/danger: an expense can
be settled correctly (success) and still be money you owe (neg). The two
scales must not collapse into each other.
settled and the two glow tokens were referenced by the design and never
declared in src/global.css. Declaring them here is what fixes that.

palettes.name: askcal
_: askcal was already consistent with the mechanical naming rule (--ink,
--line, --page), which is why its naming won and the other five sets were
renamed to match it rather than the other way round.
Renames applied: ask-* -> accent-*. brand-* was already correct.
success did not exist. It is derived from the brand ramp rather than
invented: conf-high already WAS brand-500 on a brand-50 ground, so the
status trio is the same three values that were already painting

shadows._: The scan FAB, tinted with the brand rather than a literal so a repalette carries it.

pending: onboarding/onboarding.css is a second, parallel design system inside this

Runtime renamed macro-* to bare protein/carbs/fat, so a class copied from

reserved._: Confidence is the product's core claim and macros are its output; neither may borrow a status colour.

palettes.name: charades
_: THE ONE DELIBERATE INVERSION of 'the wireframe is the spec'.
charades' wireframe ramp sat one full step off the shipped app's —
wireframe navy-500 (#2a4a85) was app navy-600 — and its own config said
so under a KNOWN DRIFT heading. charades is live, so moving the app would
change a released product's colours; moving the wireframe changes nothing
a user sees. The wireframe moves. This is written down here and on
/design/drift rather than done quietly.
Renames applied: navy-* -> brand-*, gold-* -> accent-*, and the ramps are
now the app's full ten stops rather than the wireframe's six.
crimson and royal were two undocumented ramps in the runtime with no
design source. They are not deleted — they turned out to BE the danger and
info families, so they are folded into danger-*/info-* and stop being
separate ramps. This is a small improvement on the approved plan, which
said to delete them; folding loses nothing and explains what they were.
status values are the app's (success #22c55e, danger #ef4444), consistent
with the wireframe-moves-to-app decision above.
skip is the game's third outcome — got it, passed, skipped. It was
declared in the wireframes and dropped from the runtime, which then
hand-rebuilt it as text-orange-700. Restoring it is part of phase 5.
Rule 01 applies hard here: a player reads the result row in about two
seconds, so no category tint may reuse the skip orange.

palettes.name: imposter
_: One hue by design, so there is no accent ramp — `accent` is optional and
imposter declares only `brand`. The green that was called accent-* IS the
brand; coal was never a brand ramp, it is the stage ladder and moves to
reserved.
imposter is dark-first. Its light theme is the paper scope (the card face
a player holds up) and `dark` is the flood scope the rest of the game runs
in. That is the correct way round for this product and the generator does
not care which one carries the lighter values.
No red anywhere, on purpose: a red warning in a social-deduction game
reads as an accusation. warn/danger/info are deliberately translucent
white. This is a product rule, not an oversight — do not 'fix' it.
Mr White was removed from the game in the v5 design pass, and src/lib/
round.ts no longer implements him, but role-mrwhite tokens still ship in
both runtime theme blocks. They are absent here, which deletes them.

shadows._: card is the player card a person holds up; press is the 3D edge under a primary button. Both are this game's feel, not a shared scale.

_: Rule 01, the strictest instance of it in the tree: green means Civilian
and black means Imposter. No category plate, no status chip and no pack
tile may be green. The single colour carrying the whole game carries
nothing if anything else can be green too.
role-imposter-fg is #3f3f46 here. The runtime had drifted to #0a0a0a.

palettes.name: plan-kid
_: 55 screens and no app yet. Its own config already said the app's theme
'must be generated from these values, not re-picked by eye' — scaffolding
it from this file is what makes that sentence true rather than hopeful.
Renames applied: teal-* -> brand-*, coral-* -> accent-*.
`teal` was not only a hue name, it was a live bug: it shadowed Tailwind's
own built-in teal scale while declaring only 6 of 10 stops, so
teal-300/400/600/800 silently resolved to stock Tailwind teal wherever
they were used. Renaming to brand-* removes the collision outright.
A scope is a token remap, same as a theme — the mechanism from rule 07.
`sensitive` desaturates the accent and the danger colour for the loss
and grief screens. A utility written against a variable follows whichever
scope it lands in, so no markup changes.

reserved._: Five life stages. They tint whole screens, so they must not collide with a status colour.

palettes.name: ritesh-firodiya
_: The site that publishes this system. It is included as a palette rather
than exempted, because a design system whose own host is the one surface
not measured by it is a brochure.
Renames applied: paper -> page, paper-2 -> muted, paper-3 -> sunken,
ink-inv -> ink-inverse, line-2 -> line-strong, accent -> brand-*.
Values are unchanged; this is a rename, not a redesign.
accent-2 (#a9452f) is LIGHTER than accent (#8a3324), so it maps to
brand-400 and not brand-600 — the ramp slot has to mean the same thing
here as it does in every other palette or the whole naming rule leaks.
No success/warn/danger/info: those four are not required, and this site
genuinely has no UI status axis. What looks like one is the release-state
scale, which is reserved below and means something else.
TWO INDEPENDENT AXES THAT MUST NOT BE CONFLATED, per the site's own
CLAUDE.md: m-* is the monetization model, live/beta/build/design is the
release state. A product can be free AND live, or subscription AND in
build. Collapsing them into one scale would make the products table lie.
The five model colours carry EQUAL weight on purpose. None of them may
read as a warning — 'this one costs money' is not a caution state, and
the moment ads or sub borrows the amber from warn, the table editorialises.
This is the same discipline as aakalan's pos/neg sitting beside
success/danger: money and correctness are different questions.

fonts._: The one surface that loads webfonts, via next/font. The core fallback stacks sit behind each.
fonts.mono: var(--font-jetbrains), ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

palettes.name: tic-tac-toe
_: The whole token contract existed only as a drawing: the wireframes declare
about thirty tokens and src/global.css was two import lines, so the app
hand-wrote slate-*/sky-*/rose-* that happened to coincide because the
design had been drawn FROM slate. Nothing enforced the coincidence.
`brand` here is the interactive blue, which is what the ramp slot means
everywhere else. The near-black #111827 was never a brand ramp — it is the
splash colour and must stay in step with app.config.ts, so it is reserved.
This app has no ramp stops other than 500. That is allowed: only `-500` is
required, and lint check 10 catches any stop that gets used without being
declared. The drift page reports ramp completeness rather than forcing
seven invented hexes.
Corrections applied from core: radius 2xl 28px -> 24px (it was the only
app where rounded-2xl differed), h1 34px -> 36px, and the desktop phone
frame it never had.

shadows._: The board tile lift. Uses the shared tint so it follows the theme.

_: Rule 01: blue is X and rose is O. Nothing else on the board may be
either. The difficulty scale is a separate reserved axis — it was being
re-invented in GameModeCard as emerald-700/amber-700/rose-700, which is
three different hues for three concepts that already had tokens.
`icon` exists because lucide takes a colour prop, not a className. It is
the one place in this system where a JS value is the only option, which
is why tokens.ts is a generated output rather than a hand-kept mirror.

gradients._: Named brand-x/brand-o, NOT mark-x/mark-o: the mark tokens are the flat glyph colour and a gradient cannot share their name. The set already used --brand-x-from/--brand-x-to for exactly this.

_: How this set's old names become canonical ones. Consumed by
scripts/migrate-screens.mjs, which rewrites the wireframes and the app
source in one pass.
vars are CSS custom properties in style= and stylesheets; classes are
Tailwind token names in class= and className=.

__raw._: Raw Tailwind palette in the app source. The light side coincides with the design values because the set was drawn FROM slate; nothing enforced it, which is the point. The DARK side does not coincide — the app invented its own dark values while the wireframe's .phone--dark scope said something else. The wireframe is the spec, so these map onto the design's dark values and the dark theme shifts slightly. Prefix-qualified keys (bg:, border:, text:) exist because white/10 is a hairline on an edge and a raised surface on a fill.

styles._: Inline declarations that needed a decision rather than a translation. Each one is a stated choice; anything not listed is left in place and counted, so the leftover number stays honest.

_: Structural CSS this product needs and the canon cannot know about.
The board is a device, like the phone frame: a fixed 3x3 grid whose
geometry is copied from src/constants/styles.ts so the wireframe and the
app agree on gap, padding and border. Expressing it as utilities would
scatter six coupled numbers across every screen that draws a board.
This is a narrow exception to rule 5, declared per set and checked: the
lint allows exactly the classes named here and nothing else. The first
version of the shim had no such hook, silently dropped these two rules,
and the board rendered as a single column on every screen.
